preconditions.description: The number of test cases q is between 1 and 10000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= k <= n <= 10**6 for n, k in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' in line])
preconditions.description: For each test case, n and k satisfy 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 10^6.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n for n, s in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' in line], [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' not in line]))
preconditions.description: The length of string s matches the given n for each test case.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in {'0', '1'} for c in s) for s in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' not in line])
preconditions.description: Each character in s is either '0' or '1'.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i*2] == 'YES' and len(output_lines[i*2+1]) == k and all(c in {'0', '1'} for c in output_lines[i*2+1])) or (output_lines[i*2] == 'NO') for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'YES' followed by a valid k-length binary string or 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i*2] == 'YES' and all(any(s[j] == t[j] for j in range(k)) for s in substrings) and (not any(t < candidate for candidate in possible_t if candidate != t))) or (output_lines[i*2] == 'NO') for i in range(q) for n, k, s in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' in line], [int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' in line], [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and ' ' not in line]) for substrings in [s[i:i+k] for i in range(n - k + 1)] for t in [output_lines[i*2+1]] for possible_t in [candidate for candidate in [''.join(map(str, bits)) for bits in product('01', repeat=k)] if all(any(s[j] == candidate[j] for j in range(k)) for s in substrings)])
postconditions.description: If 'YES', the output string t is lexicographically smallest and bit-similar to all substrings of s of length k; otherwise, 'NO' is printed when no such t exists.
